msdos: DIR: /P /W only in 4.0 (no /S /A /O /B); header = volume label + serial + "Directory of %1"; 8+3 name columns, "<DIR>" marker, "%1 File(s)" + "%1 bytes free" footer; /P pauses via "Press any key to continue . . ."; no-match = "File not found"
linux: POSIX ls: -R recursive, -l long, columns by tty width; no built-in paging; exit 0/>0
tinyos_decision: canonical list; /S<->-R, /W column, /P paged. DIVERGENCE: DOS 4.0 DIR has no /S -- recursion is a post-4.0 DIR feature; TinyOS adopts it deliberately

msdos: CD/CHDIR: no switches; error "Invalid directory"
linux: POSIX cd: builtin, CDPATH, cd - ; error "No such file or directory"
tinyos_decision: canonical change-dir, both spellings

msdos: CD with no arg (or CD d:) prints "D:\path"
linux: pwd (also cd with no arg goes HOME -- different!)
tinyos_decision: CD no-arg prints cwd in both flavours (DOS semantics win for the no-arg form; POSIX users get pwd)

msdos: COPY: /A /B /V per-operand; + concatenation; SILENTLY OVERWRITES -- no confirmation prompt anywhere in 4.0 COPY.ASM; "%1 File(s) copied"; recursion only via external XCOPY (/A /D /E /M /P /S /V /W, F-or-D prompt, /P per-file "(Y/N)?")
linux: POSIX cp: -r recursive, -i interactive prompt (not default); silent overwrite is also the POSIX default
tinyos_decision: canonical copy; /S<->-r tree copy. DIVERGENCE from both references: G-SEC-5 labels survive every copy, and clipboard transfers are the same verb class (EPIC-P2 5, 6.2)

msdos: ABSENT: MOVE does not exist in MS-DOS 4.0 (not in COMTAB, no source dir); REN renames in place only, 2 operands, "Duplicate file name or file not found"
linux: POSIX mv: rename or move-to-dir, disambiguated by dest; -i optional
tinyos_decision: canonical move/rename bound to MOVE and REN. DIVERGENCE: the MOVE binding is a post-4.0 DOS-ism (DOS 6+) adopted for operator muscle memory, not 4.0 parity

msdos: DEL/ERASE: /P only; all-wildcard (*.*) => "All files in directory will be deleted!" + "Are you sure (Y/N)?"; /P per-file ",    Delete (Y/N)?"; no /S in 4.0
linux: POSIX rm: -r recursive, -f force, -i prompt; no default confirmation
tinyos_decision: canonical delete; /S<->-r STILL requires confirmation policy in interactive sessions; scripts need an explicit non-interactive flag (cli-compatibility-mvp Safety). Stricter than both references by design

msdos: MD/MKDIR: no switches; "Directory already exists" / "Unable to create directory"
linux: POSIX mkdir: -p parents; "File exists"
tinyos_decision: canonical make-dir, both spellings

msdos: RD/RMDIR: no switches; "Invalid path, not directory, or directory not empty"; cannot remove current dir
linux: POSIX rmdir: empty only; rm -r for trees
tinyos_decision: canonical remove-dir; non-empty removal requires explicit recursive flag in BOTH flavours (stricter than rm -r alone)

msdos: TYPE: no switches; wildcards rejected ("Invalid filename or file not found"); stops at first ^Z; no paging
linux: POSIX cat: multi-file concatenation, -n; no ^Z semantics
tinyos_decision: canonical view-file; MVP is sequential dump, no multi-file concatenation; ^Z-stop NOT adopted (no CP/M inheritance to honour)

msdos: FIND: /V /C /N; string must be double-quoted, one string only; per-file heading "---------- file"; ERRORLEVEL 0 ok, 2 error -- level 1 (no match) defined but NEVER ASSIGNED in 4.0; errors to STDERR prefixed "FIND: "
linux: POSIX grep: regex, many flags; exit 0 match / 1 no match / 2 error
tinyos_decision: canonical find-text; literal + basic wildcard only at MVP, full regex later. Exit-code convention: adopt the POSIX 0/1/2 triple, which 4.0 FIND documents but fails to implement

msdos: SORT: /R reverse, /+n column; 64K input ceiling; ERRORLEVEL 0/1; "SORT: " STDERR prefix
linux: POSIX sort: -r -k -n etc.; no size ceiling
tinyos_decision: canonical sort-stream; bounded-memory implementation is a TinyOS requirement (fixed-capacity doctrine), so a documented input ceiling is honest DOS heritage -- but the bound is declared, not 64K-because-segments

msdos: MORE: no switches; "-- More --" on STDERR; any key continues (reads via STDERR dup after CLOSING stdin handle 0); screen size from ANSI IOCTL else 25x80 default; ^Z stops
linux: POSIX more: space/enter paging, /pattern search; less is the modern default (not MVP)
windows_terminal: terminal itself does not page -- scrollback replaces paging for interactive use
tinyos_decision: canonical page = more, not full less. The keyboard source question MORE solved by handle games is solved properly by the tab host: input routed to the focused tab only (EPIC-P2 6.3)

msdos: TREE: /F files, /A ASCII graphics; default graphics C0/C4/C3/B3, /A gives \ - + |; "Directory PATH listing for Volume %1"; ERRORLEVEL 0/1/2/3 (3 = Ctrl-Break)
linux: tree (not POSIX; common util): -a -d -L; unicode line art with ASCII fallback
tinyos_decision: canonical tree-view; the /A degrade-to-ASCII rule is generalised by EPIC-P2 6.5 rule 2: ASCII is the CANONICAL form for Reports, graphics are the enhancement

msdos: ATTRIB: +R -R +A -A, /S recurse; 16-col attribute display; exit code DISCARDED in 4.0 (C exit() with no argument -- PTM 3588 comment); "Are you sure (Y/N)?" only for code-page mismatch
linux: ls -l permission column; chmod -- multi-user mode model
tinyos_decision: attrib-view maps R/H/S/A to a capability-scoped view, NOT a POSIX UID/GID/mode triad (cli-compatibility-mvp Non-goals); every verb returns a meaningful exit code (the 4.0 discard is a counter-example)

msdos: SET: exactly one =, SET alone dumps env, NAME= deletes, "Out of environment space", COMSPEC special-cased; PATH: PATH ; clears, no-arg prints PATH=value, "No Path" when empty
linux: POSIX env/export/echo $VAR; unset; PATH colon-separated
tinyos_decision: canonical env-get/env-set; %VAR% and $VAR expansion both supported by the parser layer; per-session (per-tab) environment, an authority boundary per EPIC-P2 6.1

msdos: ECHO ON/OFF flag (default ON); ECHO alone prints "ECHO is on/off"; ECHO text prints raw line from offset 82h preserving case/spacing; @ prefix suppresses; pipes force echo off
linux: POSIX echo: -n, escape handling varies (famously non-portable)
tinyos_decision: canonical echo; batch echo semantics stay DOS-flavoured (.TCB inheritance); untrusted expansion output is rendered inert before display (EPIC-P2 6.5 rule 3)

msdos: CLS: probes INT 2F for ANSI.SYS -- if installed emits ESC[2J; if stdout redirected emits the ANSI string into the file; else INT 10h scroll+cursor-home
linux: clear/tput clear: emits terminfo sequence (ESC[H ESC[2J or E3 variant)
windows_terminal: terminal interprets ED sequences in the VT parser
tinyos_decision: canonical clear-screen; emitted as a VT sequence interpreted by the tab host renderer -- never direct video access from a session (the tab is not the screen owner, EPIC-P2 6)

msdos: VER: "Microsoft DOS             Version %1.%2"; no switches
linux: uname -a / os-release
tinyos_decision: canonical version-info; reports TinyOS version + build provenance (subset of uname -a)

msdos: VOL: "Volume in drive %1 is %2" / "has no label" + "Volume Serial Number is %1-%2"; LABEL is a separate external command
linux: df: mount table, sizes, use%
tinyos_decision: canonical volume-info; reports TinyOS storage/partition info, not a POSIX mount table (cli-compatibility-mvp). Blocked hardest by LE-48: no filesystem exists

msdos: MEM: /PROGRAM /DEBUG; address/name/size/type table; "%1 bytes total memory" summary lines
linux: free / /proc/meminfo
tinyos_decision: canonical mem-info; reports RT memory POOL usage (Design Pillar 1), not a general heap -- the DOS table shape (name/size/type rows + summary) is the adopted output model

msdos: no DOS analog in 4.0 (confirmed: nothing in COMTAB or CMD/ externals)
linux: ps / top
tinyos_decision: new canonical verb backed by the ACI-visible RT task table; DOS flavour gets a TASKMGR-style command by convention; TASKMGR full-screen view is a TAB, not an app (EPIC-P2 6)

msdos: no DOS analog in 4.0
linux: kill/signal model
tinyos_decision: new canonical verb; ACI-gated; RT-critical tasks require supervisor scope, never operator (cli-compatibility-mvp Safety)

msdos: single synchronous path: INT 10h/BIOS teletype writes straight into the text-mode video buffer; the writer IS the renderer; a slow screen blocks the program
linux: kernel VT: tty line discipline + console driver, still largely synchronous; GUI terminals decouple via pty
windows_terminal: TextBuffer decoupled from Renderer: writer calls NotifyPaintFrame() -- a relaxed atomic store, never a wait; render thread coalesces N writes into one frame ("picked up and ignored. We're about to render a frame after all")
tinyos_decision: REQUIRED, not optional: a renderer that can be starved independently of the buffer, because 6.6's drop-frames-not-block obligation is inexpressible without the seam (LE-53(b) promoted this from "worth copying" to requirement)

msdos: none: every write paints immediately; no frame concept
linux: compositor/terminal dependent
windows_terminal: render thread throttles itself (~60FPS Sleep(8)) OUTSIDE the console lock; GPU backpressure absorbed by frame-latency waitable object, also outside the lock; renderer failure backs off and disables rather than aborting
tinyos_decision: tab host and GUI mode run BELOW the real-time floor, preemptible, drop frames rather than block, and a dropped frame is REPORTED as dropped (6.6) -- stronger than WT, which drops silently by design

msdos: none: scrolled-off text is gone (BIOS scroll discards)
linux: VT softscroll historically; GUI terminals hold history
windows_terminal: circular buffer sized viewport+scrollbackLines at creation (no growth); when full the oldest row is recycled in place, O(1), no allocation ("infinite scrollback" is an open upstream TODO)
tinyos_decision: bounded fixed-capacity scrollback per the capacities doctrine (no unbounded growth on an RT system); WT's fixed-allocation circular buffer is the adopted shape; serial capture remains the unbounded record

msdos: fixed 80x25 (mode change = clear); no reflow concept
linux: VT: no reflow; GUI terminals vary
windows_terminal: full out-of-place reflow: contents copied old->new buffer, wrap flags re-evaluated, cursor remapped; alt-buffer resize deferred until return to main buffer
tinyos_decision: adopt reflow-on-resize for the tab host as interaction model; bounded work obligation applies (a reflow is O(buffer), schedulable below the RT floor, preemptible)

msdos: BIOS teletype wraps at column 80 and scrolls; no wrap-state memory
linux: VT wraps with deferred-wrap (VT100 quirk); reflow absent
windows_terminal: per-row wrap flags stored in the buffer (re-evaluated on reflow) -- wrapping is buffer state, not just cursor behaviour
tinyos_decision: wrap state lives in the buffer so reflow and serial capture agree; deferred-wrap VT quirk honoured by the VT interpreter for compatibility

msdos: optional: ANSI.SYS device driver; COMMAND probes for it per-command (CLS); most output is BIOS calls, not sequences
linux: VT/ANSI is the native console language; terminfo abstracts
windows_terminal: full VT FSM (Ground/Escape/CSI/OSC/DCS states, dedicated fuzzers); semantic dispatch layer; sixel, soft fonts, macros
tinyos_decision: VT/ANSI is the tab-session transport language (serial log = same bytes); UNTRUSTED TEXT IS RENDERED INERT before display -- filenames carrying escape sequences must not move the cursor or repaint the trusted region (6.5 rule 3, the test plants escapes in a filename)

msdos: INT 21h buffered input straight to the program; Ctrl-C polled by DOS; no host layer; any TSR sees everything
linux: kernel delivers to foreground pty; SAK (Alt+SysRq+K) exists but is root-oriented
windows_terminal: host intercepts BEFORE the app: Ctrl-C never enters the input buffer (signal path is separate and async), host-owned shortcuts checked first, keybindings dispatched before TrySendKeyEvent; but NO trusted path -- tab content can paint anything
tinyos_decision: a reserved window region NO tab content can ever paint + a secure-attention key handled by the host before any tab sees input + input routed to the focused tab only (6.3). WT's interception ORDER is the adopted shape; the trusted path is the part WT does not have and TinyOS must design

msdos: single session, no tabs; every program has the machine
linux: terminal tabs share the user's uid; no boundary
windows_terminal: explicit counter-example: every tab inherits the user's full access token; opening a tab is free; WT does not claim to be a security boundary
tinyos_decision: a tab IS an authority boundary: own ACI session identity, own flavour, own audit actor; no tab enumerates or acts for another; closing transfers nothing (6.1). Take WT's interaction model, never its authority model (6.4)

msdos: none
linux: X selections/clipboard, no label model
tinyos_decision: copy/paste/drag between tabs are cross-session transfers in the same class as COPY/MOVE: G-SEC-5 labels survive, quarantine travels with pasted content; a label-stripping clipboard is a laundering path (6.2)

msdos: none: programs write the screen directly; redirection exists only for handles
linux: pty is the universal seam; termios
windows_terminal: ConPTY: double-buffered async VT bridge -- conhost never blocks on the terminal draining the pipe (front/back buffers + OVERLAPPED WriteFile, ERROR_IO_PENDING)
tinyos_decision: the tab-session transport is the same seam class: session produces VT bytes, host buffers and renders; producer never gated on the renderer (composes with window:buffer-renderer-seam); serial fixtures are the degenerate one-way case today

msdos: n/a
linux: bidirectional serial consoles are standard (getty on ttyS0)
tinyos_decision: TODAY: TinyOS serial is TX-only -- hal-x86_64 serial.rs implements write_byte/write_bytes only, no RX path exists, no fixture reads input; the Stage E console's send_line verb resolves through the signed manifest and then reports the one-way transport honestly. Bidirectional serial is prerequisite to every live row in this register
evidence: os/src/hal-x86_64/src/serial.rs; stage E smoke evidence in REPORT-2026-07-29-04; LE-55

msdos: no DOS analog in 4.0 (COMTAB has no audit-journal command; the OS keeps no audit trail at all)
linux: ausearch / journalctl -- separate audit-query tools, not shell builtins; no POSIX shell verb renders the kernel audit stream
tinyos_decision: new canonical verb bound to SPOOR (DOS flavour): renders the session-visible spoor journal oldest-first as deterministic fixed-width columns (# CATEGORY ACTOR ACTION OUTCOME TARGET COST); first line names the journal source ("Spoor journal (<source>):"); an empty journal answers "No spoors journaled"; the shell core renders from an injected SpoorView so it stays kernel-free -- the parity lane (host golden and QEMU fixture alike) injects the policy-seam denial journal, host tabs inject their own view and say host-side journal (honest, not blurred); ACI-gated deny-by-default like every verb (LE-56, hand-2026-07-30/04A section 1.6)
